title: Let a metered fare listener be unsubscribed

blocks.text: The fare service wraps every fare listener in a metered proxy before subscribing it, so the dashboard can show how often each listener is called. Since metering went in, two things are wrong. Closing a price-alert screen calls `unsubscribe` with the same reference that subscribed, and the screen's listener keeps being told about fares. And the dashboard shows `toString`, `equals` and `hashCode` calls next to `fareChanged`.
`Metering.metered(...)` already counts calls and passes them to the listener. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Metering.java`:

items: `isObjectMethod(...)`: which calls the proxy answers itself instead of counting and passing on;

blocks.text: When you're done, a metered listener can be unsubscribed with the reference that subscribed it, a log line that prints it names the listener it meters, and the counts hold only calls made through the `FareListener` interface. About six lines in total.

cases.says: each fare change reaches the listener through the proxy and is counted under its method name
unsubscribing the metered listener with the reference that subscribed it removes it, so it hears no later fares
printing the metered listener names the listener it wraps, and returns
subscribing, printing, hashing and unsubscribing the proxy add nothing to the counts

origin.section: equals, hashCode and toString Reach the Handler Too, So the Handler Decides the Proxy's Identity

concepts: equals, hashCode and toString reach the handler; forwarding equals to the target makes the proxy unequal to itself, so a list can't remove it, and the handler should answer them itself.
Whatever the handler does with its proxy argument goes back through invoke, so printing proxy inside the handler recurses until StackOverflowError.
